content: The bigger Netflix gets, the easier it is to miss stuff. This is true of all digital platforms, of course, but it’s especially true of Netflix of late, as the streaming service’s lineup now also includes a growing library of reality shows, live-programming, and even games. It makes it easy for some of the best shows to zoom right past you, unnoticed — which almost happened to me with Midnight Diner. If you haven’t seen it, Midnight Diner is probably the most comforting thing available on Netflix. The show follows the patrons of a cozy little restaurant tucked away in the backstreets of Shinjuku, which is only open during the unusual hours of midnight to 7:00AM. This, in turn, attracts a unique blend of customers, who help each other out under the watchful eye of the shop’s owner (Kaoru Kobayashi), known only as “master.” The show aired for three seasons on Japanese TV, before being picked up by Netflix for a handful more under the subtitle Tokyo Stories. What’s especially notable about the show’s return is the huge gap: season 2 of the Netflix iteration streamed in 2019, and it took seven years for it to come back. The break was so long that season 3’s first episode, which premiered in October, is about the restaurant’s struggles during the pandemic. There are a bunch of cute scenes of the diner’s regulars sneaking outside to check if the restaurant is open yet, and wondering if it will ever be able to. If nothing else, the break was a chance for the reliable master to finally take a vacation. [Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q9E0WkC8quc] But once Midnight Diner’s new season gets going, it’s right back to everything that made it beloved. Each episode uses a different dish as a way of exploring a particular story. An overworked manga artist imagines the life he missed out on over plates of spicy konjac, while a pair of old friends reconnect while munching on pork cutlet sandwiches. What’s remarkable about the show is the way it balances being a charming, comforting watch with exploring truly difficult and heartbreaking topics. It’s the combination of sweetness and sadness that makes it work so well. It’s as likely to make you laugh as it is to make you cry. And unlike most Netflix series, the whole season isn’t streaming all at once. Instead, new episodes come out every Tuesday; so far six of a planned 10 episodes are available. It’s a welcome way to spend an evening, as the show’s slow pace and warm sense of humanity can feel like all-too rare traits in the current streaming landscape. But the main reason I’m even writing about Midnight Diner’s return is that it has been so easy to miss. There’s been next to no promotion for it — all I could find was a trailer on Netflix’s Japanese YouTube channel — and I only happened upon it accidentally after the initial premiere while browsing aimlessly through Netflix’s new releases. This, despite being someone who has watched and rewatched the previous seasons multiple times. You’d think I’d get a notification or something. Netflix has always been full of hidden gems, but now that it’s busier than ever, those gems are all the more hidden.

chineseContent: Netflix 规模越大，就越容易错过内容。当然，所有数字平台都是如此，但最近的 Netflix 尤其如此，因为流媒体服务的阵容现在还包括不断增长的真人秀、现场节目甚至游戏库。它让一些最好的节目很容易在你不注意的情况下从你身边掠过——这几乎发生在我的《午夜晚餐》中。如果您还没有看过，《午夜食堂》可能是 Netflix 上最令人安慰的节目了。该剧讲述了新宿后街一家舒适小餐厅的顾客们的故事，这家餐厅只在午夜至早上 7:00 的不寻常时段营业。这反过来又吸引了一群独特的顾客，他们在店主（小林薰饰）（只被称为“大师”）的注视下互相帮助。该剧在日本电视台播出了三季，之后又被 Netflix 以“东京故事”为副标题再播放了几季。该剧的回归尤其值得注意的是巨大的差距：Netflix 迭代的第二季于 2019 年播出，花了七年才回归。休息时间太长，以至于第三季的第一集（于 10 月首播）讲述了餐厅在大流行期间的挣扎。有很多可爱的场景，食客的常客偷偷溜到外面检查餐厅是否营业，并想知道它是否能够营业。不出意外的话，这次休息也是可靠的主人终于可以放假的机会了。 [媒体：https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q9E0WkC8quc] 但是，一旦《午夜食堂》的新一季开始，它就会回到让它深受喜爱的一切。每集都使用不同的菜肴作为探索特定故事的方式。一位过度劳累的漫画家想象着他的生活
